question: Why does this teaching present the whole range up to Śiva without rejecting other manifestations?
premises: The text on concentrations teaches the range up to Śiva through many divisions.
Unlike in other systems, nothing manifested here is denied its reality.
For those abiding in the level of truth, nothing can fall into a merely rejectable level.
inference: Because all manifestations are grounded in truth, the teaching can include the whole range without treating any part as ultimately rejectable.
plain_english: The teaching on concentrations sets out the whole range up to Śiva in many divisions. Here, unlike in other systems, nothing that appears is unreal; so for those who abide in truth, what could possibly fall into the category of what must be rejected?
